page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 7R32 processors. The system delivers 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is paired with 128 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, providing a strict 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cryptographic acceleration is present via AES and SHA-NI extensions, although advanced vector instructions such as AVX-512 and AMX are not supported.

Integrated directly into the instance is 2,400 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD local instance storage alongside a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The absence of dedicated GPU hardware establishes the node strictly for CPU-bound tasks. In synthetic benchmarks, the platform demonstrates strong multi-threaded and encryption performance, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 55,685.24 and an encryption score of 68,385.19. Single-thread execution registers lower relative throughput, with stress-ng single-core performance falling into the lower distribution tier, while Geekbench multi-core and compilation tasks show consistent median-tier output.

The 1:2 memory profile and high core density offer resource efficiency for scalable parallel execution rather than memory-heavy in-memory analytics. Bundling 2,400 GB of fast local scratch storage without remote storage latency penalties makes this instance configuration appropriate for batch compute pipelines, distributed CI/CD build farms, video encoding, ray tracing tasks, and temporary data transformation layers.
description: Amazon Web Services c5ad.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server configured with 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at 3.3 GHz. It features 128 GB of DDR4 memory, delivering a compute-centric 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 2,400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 20 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth via the AWS Nitro System. Benchmarks highlight strong performance in PassMark CPU extended instructions and hardware encryption tests, balanced by median multi-core output across standard Geekbench and compression suites. Lacking specialized GPU accelerators and AVX-512 extensions, this instance offers density-focused CPU resources and high-throughput local disk storage suited for continuous integration build runners, batch processing, ray tracing, and high-frequency data transformation workflows.
